subject: Tailwind: deployment-mode clarification & next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@tailwindretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Tailwind: deployment-mode clarification & next steps

Hi Patricia / Carlos —

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap + two concrete asks so we can land the right pilot.

Recap (from our notes):
- Business flow in scope: checkout validation + personalization + fraud-check hints (latency-sensitive at checkout).
- Observed baseline traffic: typical message ~120–180 tokens, average sustained QPS ~80, predictable daily peaks ~120 QPS, occasional bursts up to ~600 QPS for short windows (~1–3 min).
- Latency targets you mentioned: goal p95 ~120ms; hard p99 threshold ~350–400ms for checkout-critical requests.
- Preference: you said Hosted API is preferred for speed of launch but you also flagged concerns about p99 guarantees and some enterprise customers that will want a VPC/private option later.

Two asks to finalize recommended deployment path:
1) Confirm which checkout paths must meet the p99 350ms hard threshold versus less critical paths where we can accept higher tail latency. If only the core checkout call needs the p99 SLA, we can target that specifically in routing.
2) Share one hour of representative live traffic (anonymized) or give us permission to run a short synthetic replay using your token-size distribution so we can bench-run hosted vs dedicated with realistic payloads.

Proposed short experiment options (pick one):
A) Hosted pilot (fastest): 2-week hosted pilot using a reserved capacity lane + KV prefix caching. We run synthetic replay and measure p95/p99 at your burst profile. If metrics meet agreed thresholds, continue on Hosted with an SLA addendum.
B) Dedicated pilot (if strict p99 at burst): 2-week Dedicated reserved pool with autoscale to cover bursts. Slower to stand up but provides predictable headroom for tail latency.

Attachments: tailwind_latency_profile.csv (your sample), redwood_pilot_checklist.pdf (pilot steps).

If you confirm which experiment you prefer and can share the sample/replay permission, we’ll schedule a bench window this week and loop in infra for an initial draft of cost estimates.

Thanks —

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

From: Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@tailwindretail.com>

Cc: Carlos Mendoza <carlos@tailwindretail.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 18:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tailwind: deployment-mode clarification & next steps

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Checkout-critical path: yes, only the final authorization call (single tokenized prompt, ~150 tokens) must hit the hard p99 threshold. Other personalization/fetch calls can tolerate higher tails (p99 <= 800ms).
- Token sizes: confirmed typical payload ~150 tokens; worst-case < 400 tokens.
- Traffic sample: we can provide an anonymized hour; attached is the tailwind_latency_profile.csv you referenced. Please treat as internal.

Preference: We would like to try option A (Hosted pilot) to move faster, provided we can validate p99 at our bursts. If hosted fails to meet the hard p99 at realistic bursts, we'll evaluate Dedicated for checkout routes.

Two questions:
1) What does the reserved capacity lane look like for Hosted? Is that a soft reservation or backed by a capacity commitment?
2) If we need Dedicated later, how long is the typical on-ramp to VPC/Private Dedicated? We have a couple of regulated partners that may require Private within 6–8 weeks.

Thanks — I’m available for a quick sync tomorrow morning before 10:30 PT to sign off on the replay window.

Best,
Patricia Gomez
Head of Engineering, Tailwind Retail
patricia.gomez@tailwindretail.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@tailwindretail.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tailwind: deployment-mode clarification & next steps

Patricia / Soojin — quick technical note on options and a recommended test plan.

Short answers to Patricia’s questions:
- Hosted reserved lane: we can provision a soft-reservation (priority scheduling + burst credit) for the pilot within hours; for SLA-backed reservations we require a short reserved-capacity agreement (usually 1–3 months minimum) which we’ll detail in the pilot SOW.
- Dedicated / Private on-ramp: Dedicated pool + Private VPC typically 3–6 weeks depending on networking (peering, firewall rules); Private on-prem can extend beyond that. If we have network contacts and preapproved IP ranges it’s faster.

Recommendation and test plan (2-step):
1) Hosted synthetic replay (2 days of testing): we’ll replay Tailwind sample across three lanes — base (avg 80 QPS), peak sustained (120 QPS), burst window (ramp to 600 QPS for 2 min windows) — and capture p50/p95/p99 across those windows. We’ll run with KV/prefix cache enabled and an instance of your real token distribution.
2) If hosted fails to achieve p99 <= 350ms for the checkout route in the burst window, we immediately stand up a Dedicated pilot (same replay) and compare tail latency and cost.

Decision criteria (to make binary):
- GREEN: Hosted meets p99 <= 350ms for checkout route under burst profile AND cost delta vs Dedicated is >25% in favor of Hosted.
- AMBER: Hosted meets p95 but p99 is 350–500ms OR cost similar; consider Dedicated for checkout route only.
- RED: Hosted p99 >500ms under burst -> recommend Dedicated.

I’ve attached redwood_sla_options.xlsx with sample reserved-lane configurations (memory/GPU mixes) and rough cost bands for pilot sizing.

If Patricia is free tomorrow 9:00–10:30 PT we can kick off the benchmark window and get ops to standby.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tailwind: deployment-mode clarification & next steps

Patricia — great, thanks for the sample and confirmation. Proposed immediate next steps so we don’t lose momentum:
1) Benchmark window: we’ll run the Hosted synthetic replay tomorrow (Thu) at 11:00 PT. Ben will publish a short test plan and measurement dashboard beforehand.
2) Decision SLA: we’ll use the decision criteria Ben outlined. If Hosted is GREEN we continue on Hosted and draft a short addendum for a reserved-lane SLA. If AMBER/RED we’ll present a Dedicated pilot proposal within 48 hours of test completion.
3) VPC/on‑ramp timeline: Marissa — can you confirm the typical timeline for getting a Tailwind VPC prepped if the pilot goes Dedicated? We’ll need IP ranges and the contact for networking.
4) Meeting to approve replay scope: Patricia, can you confirm availability for a 15-min sign-off call at 10:45 PT today? If that works we’ll lock the 11:00 PT replay.

Links/docs: pilot checklist + ops runbook — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1qW_tailwind-pilot-resources

Thanks again, looking forward to getting metrics quickly.

Best,
— Soojin
